standard.title: Develop inquiry questions
standard.description: develop questions about objects, people, places and events in the past and present
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y1 (AC9HS1S01): Students developed questions about objects, people, places and events in past and present using Where/What/How/Why stems, and identified appropriate sources.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop questions about objects, people, places and events in the past and present to guide inquiry.

nodes.label: Historical and geographical inquiry questions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop inquiry questions about historical sites and places using a range of question stems, including perspective-seeking stems.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least three inquiry questions about a historical site or place using at least two different question types.
nodes.typical_width: Develop inquiry questions about historical sites (condition, purpose, use, importance, users) and places (features, distance, accessibility, connections); use stems including 'How do I feel about...?', 'What would it be like to...?' and 'What effect...?'
wider: Develop questions that specifically seek First Nations Australian perspectives on a local site or place
Evaluate a set of inquiry questions and revise those that cannot be answered from available sources

response_modes.reason: Year 2 introduces perspective-seeking question stems — practise across both historical and geographical contexts to build transferable questioning skill.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Perspective-seeking questions (How do I feel about...? What would it be like to...?) open up genuine empathetic inquiry — these are qualitatively richer than factual questions and support historical empathy development.
success_criteria: Develops at least two inquiry questions about a historical site or place
Uses at least one perspective-seeking stem alongside factual stems
